text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
British adventurer CHARLES LEDGER was born in 1818. He smuggled 256 alpacas, llamas and vicunas from Peru, via Bolivia, Argentina and Chile, to New South Wales.
Australian writer EDWARD DYSON, noted as the first Aussie freelance journalist to make a good living, was born in 1865.
The Reverend JOHN BARBER, organiser and promoter of the Royal Flying Doctor Service, was born on this day in 1873.
British author ALAN SILLITOE was born in 1928.

UK singer SHAKIN' STEVENS (MICHAEL BARRATT) was born in 1948. In 1980 he had a hit with "This Ole House" and went on to have further chart appearances with "Green Door" (1981), "A Love Worth Waiting For" (1984), "Merry Christmas Everyone" (1985) and with BONNIE TYLER "A Rockin' Good Way" (1984).
Scottish soccer player and manager KENNY DALGLISH, was born in 1951.

British singer, guitarist and songwriter CHRIS REA was born in 1951. He was voted "Newcomer of the Year" in 1978 in the United States. His hits included "Fool If You Think It's Over" (1978), "Stainsby Girls" (1985), "Let's Dance" (1987), "On The Beach Summer '88" (1988) and "Road To Hell, Part 2" (1989).
Australian Rugby League star RAY PRICE was born in 1953.
** EVENTS **
1634 : SAMUEL COLE opened the first tavern in Boston.
1853 : The first steamship (MARY ANN) cruised down the
Murray River.
1861 : ABRAHAM LINCOLN was sworn in as the 16th President
of a Federation of States, united only by name as the country stood on the brink of civil war.
1873 : The New York DAILY GRAPHIC became the first
illustrated daily newspaper.
1882 : The first electric trams ran in London.
1908 : The New York Education Board banned the whip as a
form of punishment in schools.
1931 : For the first time ever the West Indies defeated
Australia in a cricket match in the fifth test in Sydney, but lost the series 4-1.
1945 : As promised, American General DOUGLAS MACARTHUR
(who said in 1942 "I will return"), returned to the Phillipines where his troops took control of Manila from Japanese forces after months of fighting.
1966 : JOHN LENNON caused an outcry by claiming in a
newspaper interview that the "Beatles are more popular than Jesus Christ".
1968 : The British Lawn Tennis Association decided to
allow professionals to play in the Wimbledon championship.
1970 : 57 people were lost when their French submarine
disappeared in the Mediterranean.
1975 : CHARLIE CHAPLIN was knighted at Buckingham Palace.
1977 : More than 1,000 people were killed when an
earthquake struck Bucharest, Romania.
1989 : POPE JOHN PAUL II branded SALMAN RUSHDIE's "The
Satanic Verses" as blasphemous.
1994 : The Australian Government formally lodged
extradition papers with Spanish authorities, seeking the return of fugitive businessman CHRISTOPHER SKASE. He later successfully appealed against extradition.
